findings.reason: the plan under-scopes the fix; the same idiom must be corrected in both copies or lifted to one owner (`tests/conftest.py`), otherwise the identical defect re-reddens a different file next time xdist ordering shifts.
findings.text: `_no_defunct_child_under_self` is duplicated byte-for-byte from `tests/test_resume_reaps_its_child.py:81`, so the xdist-order defect §58 describes (a prior test in the same worker process leaves an exited, unreaped child and the whole-process `os.waitpid(-1, os.WNOHANG)` sweep trips on it) is present in the twin file too, and §58's done-when reaches only the first copy — the per-pid machinery it wants already exists as `_wait_reaped(*pids)` in this same file

findings.reason: §21 must reuse `_unresolved_citations` in `promotion.py` for the presented branch (not re-derive the list) and §22/check-manifest should extend `promotion.py`'s resolver rather than keep the `reports.py` fork, so one store probe answers every citation check; a second resolver drifts on the empty-tree and canonical-vs-raw cases the plan's own §21 tests pin.
findings.text: commit-citation resolution already has an owner at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:476` (`_commit_resolves_in`, with `_commit_canonical_id` and `_unresolved_citations` beside it), yet `reports.py` defines its own `_commit_resolves_in` rather than importing it, even though `reports.py` lazily imports three private helpers from `promotion.py` elsewhere (`_COMMITLESS_ROLES`, `_manifest_cites_a_commit`, `_repository_scope_paths`) — so §21's report branch and §22's check-manifest read the store through two independent resolvers

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — neither live section adds a module; §21 extends `_require_gate_evidence` in `reckon/crew/promotion.py` and §58 edits one test helper, so there is no new interface to measure for depth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §58 repairs one of two verbatim copies of `_no_defunct_child_under_self`, and the citation checks for §21/§22 sit beside a forked commit resolver in `reckon/crew/reports.py`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §58 names the exact helper and line it changes (`_no_defunct_child_under_self`, ~line 91), and §21 names the two pinning tests and the decision it waits on, so both proposals cite the existing mechanism rather than adding a subsystem.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper is proposed; §21 changes an existing comparison in place and §58 changes an existing assertion in place, so there is no layer to justify.
